traits.note: Cladonia (Wikipedia, Cladonia and Podetium, read 2026-11-08): a primary thallus of scales (squamules) on the ground bearing hollow upright podetia, pointed, club-like, cupped (scyphi) or branched; two morphological groups, the Cladonia morpho-type (squamulose, cup-bearing, most species) and the Cladina morpho-type (the mat-forming reindeer lichens); podetia grow 1 to 15 mm a year. The photobiont of C. rangiferina is Trebouxia irregularis or Asterochloris (Wikipedia, Cladonia rangiferina).

traits.anchorage.note: Reindeer lichens need a little soil to stay put but rarely grow on it directly, taking water and nutrients from the air (Wikipedia, Cladonia arbuscula, read 2026-11-08); lichens hold by fungal threads, neither roots nor rhizoids.

traits.substrates.note: Munger 2008, FEIS Cladonia (Cladina) spp.: on soil, humus, rock and rotting wood; south Puget Sound prairies on gravelly outwash soil (Calabria et al. 2016). Bark for the cup lichens (Wikipedia, Cladonia arbuscula: also on trees).

traits.light.note: Reindeer lichens are shade intolerant and rarely grow under 70% canopy cover or more (Wikipedia, Cladonia arbuscula, read 2026-11-08); open, well-drained ground (Wikipedia, Cladonia rangiferina).

traits.moisture.note: Cool, dry sites; they avoid standing water and keep to the driest spots of wet ground (Wikipedia, Cladonia arbuscula, read 2026-11-08); excessively drained outwash prairies (Calabria et al. 2016).

traits.podetium_cups.note: The Cladonia morpho-type, most species, bears cups; the reindeer lichens do not (Wikipedia, Cladonia, read 2026-11-08).
